usedExampleAnchors: the-like-switch-ch01: Friendship = Proximity x (Frequency + Duration) x Intensity
the-like-switch-ch03: The Golden Rule of Friendship
usedHookFrames: the-like-switch-ch01: White gloves beside a tray of coins show why contact can stay thin until one moment finally carries weight.
the-like-switch-ch02: The elevator doors open, and one step too close can turn help into pressure before a word is spoken.
the-like-switch-ch03: A glove wrapper on an ambulance floor can teach more about liking than a perfect story about yourself.
the-like-switch-ch04: Mud on shift cards shows why crossing paths every morning can still leave two crews cold.
the-like-switch-ch05: A ringing phone beside a surgery board can turn empathy into either relief or another script.
the-like-switch-ch06: Bottled water stacked beside route cards can reveal the quiet ground two strangers already share.
the-like-switch-ch07: A flickering headlamp on wet gravel can reveal the moment history starts replacing care.
the-like-switch-ch08: An unsigned contract beside a bright color palette can feel like opportunity before it has earned trust.
usedCounterFrames: the-like-switch-ch01: A weak bond is rarely fixed by adding vague friendliness. You need to see which lever is missing: access, repetition, time, or emotional weight.
the-like-switch-ch02: Approachability is not louder warmth. It is lower threat: small signals that let the other person stay in control of the first seconds.
the-like-switch-ch03: Trying to impress often steals the very feeling that makes people return. The stronger move is to help them feel capable, seen, or useful.
the-like-switch-ch04: Attraction deepens when contact starts to travel both ways. Repetition begins the path, but reciprocity decides whether it keeps going.
the-like-switch-ch05: Helpful advice often arrives too early. Rapport grows when the first response proves you heard the feeling before you move toward the fix.
the-like-switch-ch06: Trust rarely grows from bigger revelations alone. It grows when real similarity and modest disclosure move at a pace both people can match.
the-like-switch-ch07: A familiar bond can look stable while its upkeep is already thinning. Durability comes from current reciprocity, early repair, and visible care.
the-like-switch-ch08: Good feeling can outrun proof. The wiser posture is guarded optimism: stay open to connection while letting trust grow only as evidence catches up.
usedTryThisNowFrames: the-like-switch-ch01: Choose one relationship that feels stalled and write four labels: proximity, frequency, duration, intensity. Circle only the weakest one.
the-like-switch-ch02: Before your next doorway greeting, stop two steps out, open your stance, give brief recognition, and wait for the other person to meet you.
the-like-switch-ch03: In your next conversation, ask one follow-up that makes the other person useful or understood, then leave your own matching story unsaid.
the-like-switch-ch04: Choose one developing bond and mark the active force: repeated contact, reciprocity, disclosure, or support. Then name the weakest piece.
the-like-switch-ch05: When someone brings you a problem today, make your first sentence name the strain you hear, then ask one follow-up before advice.
the-like-switch-ch06: Name one real shared constraint with someone you are getting to know, then offer one modest detail at the same depth you would welcome back.
the-like-switch-ch07: Name one relationship running on history. Within a day, make one act of current repair or reciprocity visible enough to be felt.
the-like-switch-ch08: Pick one trust decision and make two columns: promising signals and verified facts. Slow only the part that still lives in the first column.
usedQuizExplanationFrames: the-like-switch-ch01.q01: They already have access and repetition. The thinness comes from contact that carries no useful emotional weight, so intensity is the missing piece.
the-like-switch-ch01.q02: The review adds duration and meaningful exchange to existing proximity. More seating only repeats nearness without changing the quality of contact.
the-like-switch-ch01.q03: Cooling means reducing the variables being fed. Coffee and warmer reassurance would add duration and intensity, which is exactly what keeps the bond active.
the-like-switch-ch01.q04: The setting needs safety before intensity. Short repeated visits build nonthreatening proximity and frequency without forcing emotional weight too early.
the-like-switch-ch01.q05: Six practices prove repetition, not belonging. The novice may need a shared task that makes the contact matter, not simply more time nearby.
the-like-switch-ch01.q06: Attendance alone can become background. A cue-reset ritual adds a purposeful exchange, which changes the contact from parallel work into mutual reliance.
the-like-switch-ch01.q07: The formula describes how bonds strengthen, not whether they deserve to. Intensity around pressure can bind the founder to the wrong influence.
the-like-switch-ch01.q08: A shared task tests whether contact has weight beyond greeting warmth. Longer greetings may add duration without proving the relationship can carry effort.

the-like-switch-ch01.q09: The shared task adds duration and modest intensity inside a safe setting. A private confession jumps past earned trust, and ignoring the bond treats the variables as invisible.
the-like-switch-ch02.q01: Stopping short protects their control while recognition lowers threat. Stepping into their path or calling loudly can turn help into pressure.
the-like-switch-ch02.q02: A visible palm and calm nod lower threat without making a performance of friendliness. The clock accuses, and the joke can feel dismissive.
the-like-switch-ch02.q03: The issue is perceived capture, not product clarity. Open posture and choice make browsing safer, while stronger claims or direct questions raise pressure.
the-like-switch-ch02.q04: The soft cues lower the social risk of the joke and give the group room to respond. Louder delivery or correction makes the newcomer feel intrusive.
the-like-switch-ch02.q05: The lowered tool and open stance reduce judgment before the story comes out. Technical explanation arrives too early, and blame closes the customer down.
the-like-switch-ch02.q06: The closed doors do not prove the policy failed. The opening stance likely made homeowners protect the doorway before they considered the content.
the-like-switch-ch02.q07: The cues may create safer seconds, but later behavior has to match them. Interrupting and pushing breaks the promise the opening made.
the-like-switch-ch02.q08: The pause, hands, and waiting lower perceived threat while respecting control. Speed, stare, closeness, or forced cheer can make the room feel less safe.
the-like-switch-ch02.q09: Recovery needs safer opening cues plus matching behavior afterward. A bigger warmth performance can feel like a mask, and arguments do not erase the first scan.
the-like-switch-ch03.q01: The second response makes the developer feel capable through a real observation. Generic praise is thin, and silent rewriting removes ownership.
the-like-switch-ch03.q02: The correct patient-care decision gives the trainee a true competence anchor. Starting with the miss may trigger defense, and vague comfort avoids the lesson.
the-like-switch-ch03.q03: Asking for help turns his observation into useful expertise. Vague gratitude is pleasant but weaker, and defending the form wastes his contribution.
the-like-switch-ch03.q04: The beginner keeps dignity while learning. A harder demo centers the instructor, and ignoring the mistake sacrifices safety for comfort.
the-like-switch-ch03.q05: Treating concerns as knowledge gives residents status in the discussion. Authority talk dismisses them, and complimenting passion dodges the substance.
the-like-switch-ch03.q06: The issue is not praise volume. The good feeling has to be grounded in a real contribution or quality, or it feels like technique.
the-like-switch-ch03.q07: The singer can hear correction while still feeling valuable to the section. The mistake is still corrected, and distraction is not the mechanism.
the-like-switch-ch03.q08: The surface question may sound warm, but the structure is self-serving. Outward attention fails when the person feels used as a route to compliance.
the-like-switch-ch03.q09: The plan protects competence while still correcting reality. Compliment padding feels artificial, and skipping the correction avoids the responsibility.
the-like-switch-ch04.q01: The group already has repeated contact. The missing piece is mutual exchange: people need to give and receive support, not just hear updates.
the-like-switch-ch04.q02: The small disclosure humanizes the moment and then returns attention to the client. The full story takes over, while silence may feel remote.
the-like-switch-ch04.q03: Attraction returns when support becomes reciprocal. Warmer thanks or more modeling can leave the same one-sided burden intact.
the-like-switch-ch04.q04: The tradeoff plus question creates reciprocal disclosure. More notes increase contact, and public praise asks for loyalty before the exchange deepens.
the-like-switch-ch04.q05: Attendance proves frequency, not attraction. A small reciprocal exchange tied to the race can make the contact feel mutual and worth repeating.
the-like-switch-ch04.q06: One-sided support makes the group attractive only for receivers. More meetings or branding would not fix the imbalance in what people give and get.
the-like-switch-ch04.q07: Disclosure helps when it is paced and reciprocal. A heavy share too early can feel like pressure rather than attraction.
the-like-switch-ch04.q08: The handoff creates reciprocal support. Same office or longer meetings may add exposure without making the relationship mutual.
the-like-switch-ch04.q09: Healthy attraction shows reciprocity across contact, disclosure, and support. Fast replies can mislead, and forced disclosure may create pressure.
the-like-switch-ch05.q01: The second sentence names the felt meaning before logistics. The others may be true, but they answer process before fear.
the-like-switch-ch05.q02: Setting down the stamp and asking next keeps attention on the apprentice's account. Immediate repair or reassurance can shut down useful details.
the-like-switch-ch05.q03: The empathic sentence fits the student's fear and then moves to action. Rules first can feel cold, and easy-to-fix reassurance may minimize the stakes.
the-like-switch-ch05.q04: The guests need the lost moment recognized before options. Kitchen detail skips emotion, and dessert may feel like a payoff without understanding.
the-like-switch-ch05.q05: Naming the fear keeps the caller engaged and helps gather better data. Schedule repetition and workload defense ignore the reason the call is hot.
the-like-switch-ch05.q06: Canned empathy points to the technique instead of the person. Length is not the core problem, and validation can support logic when it is specific.
the-like-switch-ch05.q07: Active listening is not parroting plus advice. The supervisor took control before understanding the emotional meaning.
the-like-switch-ch05.q08: The actor is risking a complaint that could prevent a stage problem. Acknowledgment keeps the report open; measurements still matter afterward.
the-like-switch-ch05.q09: The plan validates without getting stuck. A fast solution may miss the real issue, and sending them away can make the person feel dismissed.
the-like-switch-ch06.q01: The route cards and checks give them a true shared working language. Childhood stories are too personal, and reassurance does not create evidence.
the-like-switch-ch06.q02: One small mistake each makes disclosure mutual and sized. More performance or pressure would deepen the imbalance.
the-like-switch-ch06.q03: The shared constraint lets parents enter safely. Worst-night stories are too heavy early, and avoiding all disclosure can make the exchange cold.
the-like-switch-ch06.q04: Protecting the soil names a real shared stake. Tenure and compromise pressure can harden factions before common ground appears.
the-like-switch-ch06.q05: Matched imperfection makes the risk reciprocal. A solo first risk exposes one person, and a slogan does not change the power of the moment.
the-like-switch-ch06.q06: Disclosure helps when paced and mutual. Heavy early sharing can feel like a demand, not an invitation to trust.
the-like-switch-ch06.q07: A small process disclosure shows that risk can be named safely. Informality alone is not trust, and follow-up is still needed.
the-like-switch-ch06.q08: Common ground has to be true enough to stand on. Forced likeness can feel like a tactic and weaken trust.
the-like-switch-ch06.q09: The best test is matched, modest disclosure plus careful response. Forced stories rush trust, and total reserve gives closeness nothing to grow from.
the-like-switch-ch07.q01: Durability needs current care. Familiarity can hide missing upkeep, while checking only new people treats maintenance as a beginner issue.
the-like-switch-ch07.q02: Returning named tasks restores reciprocity. Public thanks may soften the imbalance, and delay lets resentment harden.
the-like-switch-ch07.q03: The second option names the maintenance gap without turning love into a courtroom. Blame escalates, and refusing to track effort hides the pattern.
the-like-switch-ch07.q04: Rotating work and repairing tone make current care visible. Music quality matters, but it will not fix the one-sided maintenance load.
the-like-switch-ch07.q05: Returned effort repairs the maintenance gap. Explanation and celebration may be sincere, but they do not change the lopsided pattern.
the-like-switch-ch07.q06: The empty shelves show maintenance has fallen behind. Storytelling may inspire, but it cannot replace present upkeep.
the-like-switch-ch07.q07: Durability depends on present reciprocity, not the age of the bond. Personality explanations can hide one-sided effort.
the-like-switch-ch07.q08: Early repair prevents drift from becoming structure. Waiting for obvious damage makes the fix larger, not smaller.
the-like-switch-ch07.q09: Current follow-up, reciprocity, and repair show living maintenance. Years and low conflict can hide passivity or avoidance.
the-like-switch-ch08.q01: The deposit and check preserve opportunity while tying trust to evidence. Starting work trusts too fast, while blanket refusal kills possible connection.
the-like-switch-ch08.q02: The bounded trial keeps openness while verifying. Friendly messages are signals, and cancellation turns caution into total suspicion.
the-like-switch-ch08.q03: Bank access needs verified evidence and staged trust. A statement adds more signal, and full access makes the test too costly.
the-like-switch-ch08.q04: The response preserves connection and safeguards. Immediate movement gives trust too fast, while blocking treats uncertainty as proof of danger.
the-like-switch-ch08.q05: References and a test order convert rapport into evidence. Exclusivity trusts the booth too much, while blanket avoidance rejects real opportunity.
the-like-switch-ch08.q06: Truth bias makes a plausible notice feel usable too soon. Checking and then warning keep trust tied to reality.
the-like-switch-ch08.q07: Verification is compatible with warmth when stakes are real. Good feeling can guide attention, but it should not replace evidence.
the-like-switch-ch08.q08: High access before verified history creates exposure. Polished samples and fast answers may be positive signals, but they are not enough for admin trust.
the-like-switch-ch08.q09: The plan keeps connection possible while pacing trust. Quick trust is naive, and withholding all warmth turns caution into suspicion.
